Switch a document's line endings and act on a tab without leaving it. More at [www.malgel.com](https://www.malgel.com).

## New

- **The line ending is a button in the status bar.** Clicking it switches the open document between LF and CRLF, the way VS Code's *Change End of Line Sequence* does. The text is untouched; the document is marked unsaved and saving writes the file with the new ending. The status bar also names the indent size (`Spaces: 2`) beside the line ending and the language.
- **Copy Path and Reveal in File Manager** in a tab's own menu, as in VS Code. Both act on that tab's file, so they appear once it has been saved.

Neither change adds a shortcut; *Change end of line sequence* is also in the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P).

## Downloads

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS 11+ (Apple silicon) | `Malgel-0.1.5-macos-arm64.dmg`: open it and drag Malgel to Applications |
| Windows 10+ | `Malgel-0.1.5-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `Malgel-0.1.5-windows-x64.zip` (portable) |
| Linux x86_64 | `Malgel-0.1.5-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or `malgel-0.1.5-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

The macOS app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so Gatekeeper blocks it after download: right-click it and choose Open once, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Malgel.app`. The Windows files are unsigned: SmartScreen may warn, and **More info → Run anyway** gets past it. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every file's checksum.
